description.cancellation_policy:
Change Policy:

Once a permit reservation is created, the permit holder may modify the campsite locations, group size, entry & exit points, vehicle information, stock numbers and emergency contact. 

The permit start date may not be modified. The existing reservation must be canceled and a new reservation must be booked. 

Cancellation Policy:

The permit holder may cancel their reservation at any point prior to it being issued. The $36 Wilderness Administrative Fee is non-refundable and non-exchangeable.

As a courtesy, visitors often notify the Wilderness Office as soon as possible if they decide not to use their reservation so that the sites may be made available for others.
description.description:
Before proceeding to plan your wilderness camping trip, please visit Rocky Mountain National Park's Wilderness Camping page. When finished, return to this page to book your trip.

Rocky Mountain National Park’s 415 square miles encompass and protect spectacular mountain environments. The park provides exceptional access to wild places for visitors to recreate and experience solitude and outstanding scenic beauty. Roads and over 300 miles of trails bring visitors to the doorstep of a variety of wilderness-based recreational opportunities and ability to enjoy viewing wildflowers, wildlife, mountain scenery and starry nights.

Congress has set aside 95% of Rocky Mountain National Park as designated wilderness. Rocky Mountain National Park is managed in a way to preserve its wilderness character for future generations.
description.driving_directions: The main area of Rocky Mountain National Park can be accessed through the park’s three main entrance stations. On the east side use the Beaver Meadows Entrance Station along US HWY 36 or the Fall River Entrance along HWY 34, both outside the town of Estes Park, Colorado. On the west side of the park use the Grand Lake Entrance Station along US HWY 34, outside the town of Grand Lake, Colorado.

description.need_to_know_permit:
Our park has a proud culture of backpackers who Leave No Trace while camping here in Rocky Mountain National Park. Thank you for joining us in the Leave No Trace ethics of minimal impact camping.

A commercial hard-sided carry-in/carry-out bear-resistant food storage canister is required from April 1 through Oct. 31. Canister must be locked and placed on the ground 70 adult steps away from campsite. Canisters may be rented or purchased at local sporting goods stores in Estes Park and Grand Lake. Plan ahead to leave no food or scented items in your vehicle at the trailhead. Arrive early for parking. Bear canisters are required for any and all overnights in Rocky's Wilderness and must be brought into the Wilderness Office in order to obtain a Wilderness Permit.

To minimize impact on the park's precious Wilderness, the number of permits issued is limited.  

Important Permit Details

Wilderness Office Hours: 7:00 a.m. - 3:30 p.m. daily.

Please review your Wilderness Campsite Reservation Confirmation and make sure your campsites and dates are correct.

Permits must be picked up in person at the Wilderness Office adjacent to the Beaver Meadows Visitor Center on Hwy 36 just west of Estes Park or at the Kawuneeche Visitor Center on Hwy 34 just north of Grand Lake. You must furnish the license plate number(s) of any vehicle(s) that will be parked at the trailhead(s).

Permits may be picked up as early as 30 days before your trip. Because parking lots fill early, we recommend picking up your permit a day or two before your trip begins so that you can get an early start on the first day of your trip. 

Wilderness Designated Sites

Individual sites: For parties of 1 to 7 people.

Each party is assigned 1 campsite. Groups over 7 persons may not camp in neighboring individual sites but must reserve group sites or split up and reserve individual sites at least 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) apart.

Group sites: For parties of 8 to 12 people.

Groups must camp at special sites. Because of impact caused by group interaction in and between sites (site spread, social trails, etc.), groups over 7 persons may not camp in neighboring individual sites but must reserve group sites or split up and reserve individual sites at least 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) apart.

From June through September, campers may stay in the Wilderness for a maximum of 7 nights with no more than 3 consecutive nights in the same campsite. 

Campfires are PROHIBITED. Use portable stoves only.

Sprague Lake Accessible Campsite

This is a special wheelchair-accessible Wilderness campsite near Sprague Lake. It is 0.5 miles (1 kilometer) from the trailhead to the campsite. The camp accommodates up to 12 campers including a maximum of 5 wheelchair users. To make a reservation, call 970-586-1242.

Wilderness Stock Sites

There are special campsites with particular rules and regulations for overnight wilderness camping with stock (horses or llamas.) Some trails are closed to stock use.

Wilderness Technical Climbing Bivouac Zones

A Wilderness Technical Climbing Bivouac is a temporary, open-air encampment (with no erected tent or shelter) for technical climbers on routes of 4 technical pitches or more. Use of pack in/pack out human waste bags are required. If you plan to bivouac, you must identify your technical climbing route and must obtain a Bivy Permit from the Wilderness Office during listed office hours.

Wilderness Technical Orienteering Cross-country Zones (No Trails)

Technical Orienteering Cross-country Zones are the least accessible and least traveled and places in Rocky Mountain National Park. The zones are reached through technical orienteering with required orienteering and off-trail navigation skills with map, compass/GPS while bushwhacking off trail, in remote areas characterized by rugged terrain, dense forests, downed trees, wet bogs and icy streams.

There are no developed trails, no developed campsites and no pit toilets. The Technical Orienteering zones are below treeline. It takes considerable additional time utilizing technical orienteering and navigation skills along the way to reach your destination than if you were on a trail. Off-trail navigation skills are required.

Those who travel here must be skilled with a map and compass/GPS and must be proficient in and dedicated to Leave No Trace camping and hiking ethics and techniques.

If you'd like to reserve a Stock, Bivy, or Cross-country Zone site, please contact the Wilderness Office to check availability as these sites are not available for online reservation.

Wilderness Winter Camping

There are special rules for overnight wilderness winter camping.

To check conditions on Longs Peak before committing to a trip in the area, please check the Longs Peak Conditions Report.

description.no_show_policy:
If the permit is not picked up by 12:00 PM noon MST the day of arrival, the visitor will be considered a "no show." The permit may be canceled and is not refundable.  

You may call prior to noon on the first day of your trip to indicate an arrival after noon, in which case your permit will be held for you until the Wilderness Office closes at 3:30pm MST. Permits may not be picked up outside of office hours.  

Call (970) 586-1242 to inform the Wilderness Office of a post-noon, pre-3:30 pm MST arrival.
description.quota_details:
Within Rocky Mountain National Park, Wilderness Overnight Backpacking is managed with quotas for designated campsites. The party size and length of stay are used to help manage use for resource protection and visitor enjoyment.

From June through September, campers may stay in the Wilderness for a maximum of 7 nights with no more than 3 consecutive nights in the same campsite.  

An individual campsite can accommodate parties of 1 to 7 people. Group campsites can accommodate parties of 8 to 12 people. Because of impact caused by group interaction in and between sites (site spread, social trails, etc.), groups over 7 persons may not camp in neighboring individual sites but must reserve group sites or split up and reserve individual campsites that are at least 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) apart.
description.season_information:
In order to preserve the extraordinary Wilderness character of Rocky Mountain National Park, you must have a Wilderness Permit for any overnight backpacking trip in the park. A Wilderness Overnight Backpacking permit is required year-round. Your permit must be picked up in person at the east side Headquarters Wilderness Office (adjacent to the Beaver Meadows Visitor Center on Highway 36 west of Estes Park, CO) or at the west side office located within the Kawuneeche Visitor Center (Highway 34, north of Grand Lake, CO). 

The Wilderness Office is open daily from 7:00am-3:30pm MST. 

Permits may not be picked up outside of office hours.

Bear canisters are required for any and all overnights in Rocky's Wilderness and must be brought into the Wilderness Office in order to obtain a Wilderness Permit.

Permits may be picked up as early as 30 days before the start date of your trip.  

Advance Reservation window opens for the Wilderness Camping Season every year on March 1st at 8 a.m. MT. Online only.

4675320033.description:
Number of Parties Permitted: 4 (1-12 people per party) 

Camp must be established: 

1. within the designated wilderness winter zone, at least 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) from the trailhead.

2. at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) away from water.

3. on snow or rock only -- never on vegetation or in meadows.

4. out of sight and sound of trails and other campers. 

5. If the designated summer campsite has more than 4 inches (10 centimeters) of snow, camp at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) away from the campsite. Do not camp in the campsite.

Camp safely away from standing dead trees. 

NO FIRES, Fires prohibited, Use portable stoves only.

Purify water.

Leave No Trace.

Number of Parties Permitted: 6 (1-12 people per party) 

Camp must be established: 

1. within the designated wilderness winter zone, at least 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) from the trailhead.

2. at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) away from water.

3. on snow or rock only -- never on vegetation or in meadows.

4. out of sight and sound of trails and other campers. 

5. If the designated summer campsite has more than 4 inches (10 centimeters) of snow, camp at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) away from the campsite. Do not camp in the campsite.

description_map.need_to_know:
Advanced Winter Mountaineering and Orienteering: Review & consider experience/conditions/hazards/equipment. Expect winter and avalanche conditions. Bring four-season winter gear.

A carry-in/carry-out bear resistant food storage container is the preferred food storage in the winter. Hanging food is permitted by the counterbalance method from November 1-March 31 only.

If the designated summer campsite has more than 4 inches (10 centimeters) of snow, camp at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) away from the campsite. Do not camp in the campsite. Camp on snow or rock only -- never on vegetation or in meadows.

Camp safely away from standing dead trees. 

NO FIRES, Fires prohibited, Use portable stoves only.

Purify water.

Leave No Trace.

A bivouac must be established:

1. within the designated Zone, or at the base or on the face of the climb.

2. at least 70 adult steps (200 feet/60 meters) from water.

3. with camp set up at dusk and taken down before dawn.

4. without the use of erected type shelters, tents or supported tarps.

5. on rock or snow only, not on vegetation and out of meadows.
